Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-895,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
The Global Carbon Budget 2026 describes the methodology, main results, and datasets used to quantify the anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) and their partitioning among the atmosphere, land ecosystems, and the ocean over the historical period (1750–2026). These living datasets are updated every year to provide the highest transparency and traceability in the reporting of CO2, the key driver of climate change.

item.title: Climatology of the sea temperature from long-term in situ observations: Northern Chilean Patagonia
item.description:
Climatology of the sea temperature from long-term in situ observations: Northern Chilean Patagonia
Cécile Pujol, Alexander Barth, Iván Pérez-Santos, Pamela Linford, and Aida Alvera-Azcárate
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8167–8189, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8167-2026, 2026
In this study, we present the first high-resolution, four-dimensional temperature climatology for Northern Chilean Patagonia, a region characterised by a complex network of fjords and channels. The climatology is based on approximately three million in situ observations collected over the past 75 years and interpolated into continuous temperature fields with a horizontal resolution of about 900 m and 32 vertical levels, providing monthly and daily fields from the surface to 400 m depth.

item.description:

Laura Bentley, Claire M. Wood, Christopher Feeney, Sabine Reinsch, Angus Garbutt, Susan Tandy, Inma Lebron, Amy Thomas, Maud van Soest, Victor Ebuele, James Lucas, M. Robinson
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-459,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
The Countryside Survey has been monitoring the environment in Great Britain for 45 years, providing unique insights into changing national conditions and drivers of change. The soils data from this program contains >8600 topsoil samples and captures the full diversity of conditions in Britain ecosystems, covering the biological, physical and chemical properties of soils. The dataset enables key questions to be addressed on soil condition, function, threats and pressures across systems at scale.

item.title: A national-wide dataset of plot-level living tree biomass and carbon stocks in Chilean native forests
item.description:
A national-wide dataset of plot-level living tree biomass and carbon stocks in Chilean native forests
Karen Sandoval-Salazar, Alejandro Miranda, Jorge Hoyos-Santillan, Rocío Urrutia-Jalabert, Timo Tokola, Carlos Hormazábal, Francoise Pincheira, Cristian Pérez, and Blas Mola-Yudego
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-720,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
This dataset provides the first baseline of native forest carbon stocks for Chile across a 2,800 km latitudinal gradient, derived from 2,024 field plots containing 59,408 living trees representing 77 species. These ecosystems include the southernmost forests on the planet, located in subantarctic Patagonia.

item.title: Annual global terrestrial ecosystem maps from 1982 to 2024 aligned with the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology
item.description:
Annual global terrestrial ecosystem maps from 1982 to 2024 aligned with the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology
Zhenrong Du, Le Yu, Xiyu Li, Hui Wu, Ruyue Chang, Alice C. Hughes, David Coomes, James G. C. Ball, Xiaorui Ma, Hongyu Wang, Huawei Wan, Jixi Gao, and Keping Ma
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-791,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Existing global ecosystem maps are often static, making long-term changes difficult to track. We produced annual maps of global terrestrial ecosystems from 1982 to 2024 by combining satellite observations aligned with the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology. Independent evaluation showed an average accuracy of 86 %. The dataset provides a consistent record for studying ecosystem change and supporting biodiversity assessment, conservation planning, and environmental policy.

item.title: High precision atmospheric GHG measurements for the Orinoco region: The Villavicencio Tower (VLO)
item.description:
High precision atmospheric GHG measurements for the Orinoco region: The Villavicencio Tower (VLO)
Stijn Hantson, Santiago Botía, Miguel Ángel Navarro-Ramírez, Diego Pardo-Buitrago, João Fernandes Amaral, Shrutika Wagh, Miguel Ángel Ramírez-Niño, Anghy Gutierrez-Rincon, Mauricio Salamanca, Armin Jordan, Steffen Knabe, Tarek El Madany, Karl Kuebler, Heiko Moossen, Michael Rothe, Christian Rödenbeck, Sönke Zaehle, and Carlos Sierra
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-831,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Northern South America may play an important role in the global greenhouse gas balance, yet no atmospheric monitoring stations cover this region. Here, we present weekly air samples collected from a tower in Colombia since 2023, with comprehensive measurements of greenhouse gases and their isotopic composition. This unique dataset will help constrain regional greenhouse gas emissions, particularly cross the orinoco plains.
